employersPage.heroTitle: Short on staff? Hire motivated foreign workers with Haken Work.
employersPage.heroLead: Haken Work connects companies in Japan with foreigners who want to work here, through staffing and placement. We take care of everything from checking residence status to support after they start.

speed.title: Fast placement
speed.body: We quickly introduce candidates who match your requirements, even for sudden staffing needs.

languages.title: Support in 6 languages
languages.body: We explain the job to staff in Vietnamese, Burmese, Nepali, Bengali and English, which prevents mismatches and early resignations.

visa.title: Residence status checked in advance
visa.body: We confirm that each person is allowed to work before introducing them, reducing the risk of illegal employment.

support.title: Follow-up after hiring
support.body: Our staff handle questions about attendance and daily life, so your on-site managers carry less of the load.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.body: Send us a message with the form below.

hearing.title: Consultation
hearing.body: We ask about the work, headcount, timing and conditions.

contract.title: Contract
contract.body: Once you accept the quote, we sign a contract.

matching.title: Introduction
matching.body: We select matching candidates and arrange interviews and site visits.

start.title: Start work
start.body: We keep following up after they start.

cost.a: It depends on the type of contract (staffing or placement), the number of people and the working conditions. Contact us and we will send a quote. Consultation is free.

visa.q: What residence statuses do your candidates have?
visa.a: We introduce people who are allowed to work, such as permanent residents, long-term residents, spouses of Japanese nationals and Specified Skilled Workers. Students can only work within their permission (generally up to 28 hours a week).

japanese.q: How well do they speak Japanese?
japanese.a: Our candidates range from everyday conversation (around JLPT N4) to business level (N2 or above). Tell us the level the job needs.

trouble.q: What if a problem happens after they start?
trouble.a: Our staff talk with the worker in their native language and help solve the problem, so your site does not have to handle it alone.

area.q: Can rural workplaces use the service?
area.a: Yes, we accept requests from all 47 prefectures. Jobs that include housing tend to attract many applicants.

employersPage.formLead: Our staff will review your message and reply within 2 business days.

form.agree: I agree that the information I entered is used according to the <link>privacy policy</link>.
form.doneBody: We have sent a confirmation email to the address you entered. Our staff will contact you within 2 business days.

faqPage.title: FAQ
faqPage.lead: Common questions about finding and applying for jobs.

free.q: Does it cost anything to register or apply?
free.a: No. Registering and applying for jobs are free.

noJapanese.q: Can I apply if I don't speak Japanese?
noJapanese.a: Yes. Some jobs need no Japanese. Use the "Japanese level" filter on the job list to show only jobs that fit your level.

abroad.q: Can I apply from outside Japan?
abroad.a: At the moment the service is for people who live in Japan and have a residence status that allows them to work.

how.a: Press "Apply" on the job page, log in (or sign up) and fill in your profile, then send your application.

cv.a: You can apply without one, but a CV speeds things up. You can upload up to 5 PDF or Word files (5MB each).

status.q: Where can I see the result?
status.a: Check your status on My page. We also email you when it changes.

cancel.q: I want to cancel an application.
cancel.a: Please contact us with the contact form.

visa.a: Your residence status decides what work and how many hours you can do. See the "Visa" page.

dormitory.a: Yes. Choose "Housing provided" under Preferences on the job list.

pay.q: When and how am I paid?
pay.a: It depends on the job and contract. Always confirm at the interview and when you sign.

password.a: Use "Forgot your password?" on the login page to get a reset email.

delete.q: I want to delete my account.
delete.a: Go to My page -> Account settings -> Delete account. Your data and CVs are deleted.

visaPage.title: About visas (residence status)
visaPage.lead: Whether you can work in Japan, and what work you can do, depends on your residence status. Check what yours allows before applying.

free.title: Statuses with no limit on the kind of work
free.body: Permanent residents, spouses of Japanese nationals or permanent residents, and long-term residents can do any kind of work for any hours, including dispatch and part-time jobs.

limited.title: Statuses that allow only certain work
limited.body: Specified Skilled Worker, Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Technical Intern Training and similar statuses allow only the permitted field and work. Before changing jobs, check that the new work is allowed. Technical interns generally cannot work anywhere other than their training site.

permission.title: Statuses that allow limited hours with permission
permission.body: Students and dependents can work generally up to 28 hours a week once they get "permission to engage in activity other than that permitted" (students: up to 8 hours a day during long school holidays). Adult-entertainment related work is not allowed.

check.card: Check "work restrictions" on the front of your residence card and the permission field on the back.
check.expiry: Apply to renew before your period of stay ends (you can apply from about 3 months before).
check.change: With a work-type status, you must notify the Immigration Services Agency within 14 days when your employer changes.

visaPage.disclaimer: This page is general guidance. For your own case, ask the Immigration Services Agency or an expert.
